title: Coherent Control of Energy Transport at Room Temperature in a Noisy Bath
abstract: Coherent control of energy transport in a non-equilibrium steady-state (NESS) in a reaction-center-connected donor-acceptor pair is proposed. The pigments are considered to be continuously interacting with incoherent radiation and a phonon bath while being driven by phase-controlled coherent fields. Coherent excitation of the donor-acceptor pair is shown to induce interference between excitation pathways, resulting in phase dependent modulation of the flux. As a consequence one can enhance or suppress energy transfer via interference, e.g. an optical energy switch. The persistence of such interference enables coherent control at a NESS in dissipative regime suggests an extension of the operational scope of quantum control from traditional transient domain with low dissiaption to noisy environment NESS at room temperature.
summary: The paper proposes using coherent laser fields to actively control the rate of energy transfer between donor and acceptor molecules in a system immersed in thermal noise. By exploiting quantum interference effects, researchers demonstrate that the energy flux can be switched or enhanced simply by tuning the relative phase of the driving lasers, proving robust control in a realistic, dissipative environment.
main_problem: The research addresses the coherent control of energy transport within a non-equilibrium steady state (NESS) in a system coupled to a noisy, dissipative environment at room temperature.
main_result: Coherent excitation can induce interference between energy transfer pathways, allowing for phase-dependent modulation—acting as an optical energy switch—even when the system is operating in a highly dissipative regime.
method: The analysis involves solving the master equation to find the NESS, utilizing theoretical frameworks like the Redfield and Lindblad approaches to model open quantum dynamics.
model_or_system: The model is a minimal donor-acceptor pair connected to a reaction center, treated as an open quantum system interacting with both incoherent radiation (pumping) and a phonon bath. The evolution is governed by a master equation incorporating various coupling terms.
key_observables: Energy flux ($F$) between the donor and acceptor sites; Donor-acceptor coherence ($	ilde{ho}_{ad}$).
important_parameters: Relative phase ($\phi$) of coherent fields, bath temperature (300 K), reorganization energy ($\lambda_b$), and coupling ratios ($\Omega/J(\Gamma)$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Markovian approximation and weak system-bath coupling. For NESS calculations, analytical solutions are often intractable, necessitating numerical methods.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate flux modulation as a function of relative phase ($\phi$) for different pumping conditions, and show how the calculated flux depends on the ratio between coherent field strength ($\Omega$) and bath spectral density ($J(\Gamma)$).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the full Hamiltonian and master equation to deriving simplified Liouvillians (system-bath and system-radiation) under approximations. It then analyzes the steady-state flux in different coupling regimes, culminating in demonstrating phase control.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it extends quantum control concepts from idealized transient dynamics into realistic, noisy, non-equilibrium steady states characteristic of biological energy conversion processes at ambient temperatures.
